plan.objective: Make account search match on email address as well as name
expectedSchemas: account object shape: { name: string, email?: string }
plan.intent: Add email-address matching to the existing case-insensitive substring account search in src/search/accounts.js, so searchAccounts returns an account when the trimmed lowercased query is a substring of either its name or its email; missing/non-string email fields must not throw, and the existing empty/whitespace-query returning [] and name-matching behavior are preserved. Extend test/search.test.js only (per README's one-test-file-per-module rule) with cases for an email-only match and an account lacking an email.

plan.objective: Add a created-at column to the CSV export
expectedSchemas: CSV export row object shape consumed by toCsv
plan.intent: Add a new createdAt column to the CSV export by appending it to the COLUMNS list in src/export/csv.js so exportColumns() and toCsv() emit it as a trailing header/field (missing values fall back to the existing empty-string default), and extend test/export.test.js to cover it; no columns are removed, renamed, or reordered, and no other module or its tests are touched.

plan.objective: Round every amount a customer is shown to whole pence so totals never display long decimals
plan.intent: Change the customer-facing rounding precision owned by src/format/money.js from whole pounds (PLACES = 0) to whole pence (PLACES = 2), so roundMoney — and everything that delegates to it, including formatMoney and orderTotal in src/pricing/total.js — yields two-decimal amounts instead of long decimals or over-rounded pounds. This adjusts existing behavior in one place rather than adding a new rounding path; no call sites, exports, or other modules (pricing/discount, pricing/tax, notify, audit, export, search) change, and a whole-pence assertion is added to the module's own test/money.test.js.

plan.objective: Retry webhook delivery up to three times when the transport reports a failure
expectedSchemas: deliver return value: { url: string, delivered: boolean } (retains existing keys; may gain an attempts count)
expectedTests: test/webhook.test.js: does not retry when the first attempt succeeds
test/webhook.test.js: retries until the transport succeeds
test/webhook.test.js: stops after three failed attempts and reports delivered false
test/webhook.test.js: webhook delivery reports the endpoint it used
plan.intent: Add retry behavior to the existing webhook deliver() function: when the injected transport reports a failure (response.ok !== true or a thrown error), re-invoke it up to a maximum of three total attempts, returning delivered:true on the first success and delivered:false after the third failure. Purely additive to src/notify/webhook.js plus new cases in test/webhook.test.js; no existing behavior, API shape, or other module is removed or disabled, and no network or external access is required since the transport is a caller-supplied function.

plan.intent: Add a new originating-IP field to audit entries by extending auditEntry with an ip parameter that is carried onto the returned entry object; no existing behavior is removed or disabled, and isPrivileged is unchanged.

plan.objective: Orders paid by card should cost an extra five percent on top of what the customer would otherwise pay
expectedApis: orderTotal(order) — reads a new order.payment field to apply a card surcharge
expectedSchemas: order object gains an optional `payment` property (e.g. { method: "card" | "cash" | ... }); absent/non-card payment must keep current totals unchanged
expectedTests: node --test (full suite: audit, discount, email, export, money, search, tax, total, webhook)
plan.intent: Add new behavior: a 5% card-payment surcharge applied in src/pricing/total.js on the full amount the customer would otherwise pay (line items after discount, plus delivery, plus tax) before rounding via roundMoney, factored into a new src/pricing/surcharge.js module mirroring the existing discount.js/tax.js pattern; non-card and unspecified payment methods keep today's totals unchanged.

plan.objective: Orders of one hundred pounds or more should not be charged for delivery, and every other order should be charged three pounds
expectedTests: a bigger basket costs more than a smaller one
an order at or above the free-delivery threshold is not charged delivery
an order below the free-delivery threshold is charged three pounds delivery
an order total is a positive number
plan.intent: Add a conditional free-delivery threshold to order pricing: in src/pricing/total.js, replace the unconditional flat DELIVERY charge with a rule that waives the three-pound delivery charge when the post-discount, pre-tax order amount is one hundred pounds or more, keeping the three-pound charge for every order below that threshold; delivery remains part of the taxable base and rounding still goes through roundMoney. Existing behavior for line items, discount, tax, and rounding is unchanged; the only pricing module touched is total.js and the only test file touched is test/total.test.js, per the repository's one-test-file-per-module convention. Note the specified rule is intentionally non-monotonic at the boundary (a 99-pound basket totals more than a 100-pound basket), so the existing "a bigger basket costs more than a smaller one" test must keep both baskets on the same side of the threshold.

plan.objective: Add a flat two pound handling charge to every order's total
plan.intent: Add behavior: introduce a new flat £2 handling charge constant in src/pricing/total.js and include it in every order's pre-tax amount alongside the existing £3 DELIVERY charge, so the handling fee is taxed and rounded the same way; add a test in test/total.test.js covering the increase. No existing charge, discount, tax, or rounding behavior is removed or disabled, and no other module or its tests are touched.

plan.objective: Orders that contain only digital goods should not be charged tax
expectedSchemas: order.lines[].digital (boolean flag marking a line item as a digital good; absent/falsey means physical)
plan.intent: Add a digital-goods exemption to tax calculation: taxFor currently ignores its order argument and always applies STANDARD_RATE; change it to return 0 when every line in the order is a digital good, leaving mixed and all-physical orders taxed as before. An order with no lines must not be treated as digital-only. src/pricing/total.js already passes order through to taxFor, so no caller changes are needed, and per README each module owns its own test file, so only test/tax.test.js gains coverage (digital-only exempt, mixed basket taxed, empty basket taxed).

plan.objective: Customers who have placed more than twenty five orders should get fifteen percent off instead of ten
plan.intent: Change existing loyalty discount behavior in src/pricing/discount.js: raise the qualifying threshold constant LOYAL_ORDERS from 10 to 25 (strictly more than 25 orders) and raise LOYAL_RATE from 0.1 to 0.15, so qualifying customers get 15% off instead of 10%. No new discount tiers, no removal of the existing rule, no signature or API change; discountRate still returns 0 for undefined customers and non-qualifying customers. test/discount.test.js is updated to pin the new threshold boundary and the 0.15 rate; src/pricing/total.js consumes discountRate unchanged, and its tests use orders:3 so they remain unaffected.
